source.title: Fabric Structure and Design
source.author: N. Gokarneshan
source.note: Page numbers below are the BOOK's printed page numbers. The PDF page is the book page + 13.
source.scope_warning: This book covers woven fabric only. It contains no weft-knitting or warp-knitting content, so it cannot supply K/T/M needle programmes, Munden Kc/Kw constants, or loop-length relations for the knit engine.

weaves.name: Plain (calico / tabby)
characteristics: maximum number of binding points
threads interlace 1 up 1 down on alternate order
thread density is limited
cloth thickness and mass per unit area are limited
strongest fabric of any simple combination of threads except gauze/cross weaving

weaves.name: Warp rib
weaves.derivation: plain weave extended in the warp direction
weaves.setting_rule: warp rib effect is enhanced by a high number of ends per inch and a comparatively low number of picks per inch

weaves.name: Weft rib
weaves.derivation: plain weave extended in the weft direction
weaves.setting_rule: weft rib requires a high number of picks per inch and a comparatively low number of ends per inch

weaves.name: Matt rib (hopsack / basket)
weaves.derivation: plain weave extended in BOTH warp and weft directions

weaves.name: Twill
characteristics: diagonal lines run from one selvedge to another
more ends and picks per unit area than plain cloth
fewer binding points than plain cloth
better cover than plain weave
more cloth thickness and mass per unit area

weaves.name: Satin / Sateen
weaves.definition: satin is a warp-faced rearranged twill; sateen is a weft-faced rearranged twill - satin is the reverse side of sateen
characteristics: either warp or weft faced
no prominent weave structure
only one binding point in each end or pick
no continuous twill lines
poor seam strength due to thread mobility
more thread density possible in warp and weft
more mass per unit area possible
fewer binding points and longer floats
construction requires move numbers (intervals of selection)

weaves.name: Corkscrew
requirements: repeat size must be an odd number
warp float must be one greater than weft float for warp-faced (and vice versa for weft-faced)
characteristics: hard weave
firm and compact texture
good strength, durability and warmth

weaves.name: Ordinary honey comb
characteristics: cell-like appearance with ridges and hollows
single line crossing a single line, or double line crossing a double diagonal line
more warp and weft floats
moisture absorbent due to floats
constructed with pointed drafts
reversible - similar effect on both sides
forms one cell per repeat

weaves.name: Brighton honey comb
characteristics: non-reversible - face differs from back
constructed on straight drafts only
repeat size is a multiple of 4
longest float is N/2 - 1 where N is the repeat size
a single diagonal line crosses a double diagonal line
forms 4 cells per repeat (two large, two small)

weaves.name: Huck a back
characteristics: repeat divided into four equal parts - two filled with plain weave, two with long float motif
plain weave gives firmness to the cloth
long float motif gives moisture absorbency

weaves.name: Crepe (crape / oatmeal)
characteristics: contain no twilled or other prominent effects
cloth covered by minute spots or seeds
highly irregular puckered surface
high twist yarns used with controlled shrinkage
construction_methods: combination of a floating weave with plain threads
insertion of one weave over another

weaves.name: Bedford cord
weaves.loom_equipment: Dobby with fast reed and heavy beat up
characteristics: longitudinal warp lines with fine sunken lines between
constructed on a pair of picks or alternate picks
face ends weave the cord, cutting ends weave plain
wadding threads never interlace with weft and need a separate, more heavily tensioned beam

weaves.name: Welts and piques
weaves.loom_equipment: Dobby with fast reed, two warp beams, drop boxes (2x1 or 2x2)
characteristics: pronounced ridges and furrows running transversely (weft way)
plain face fabric plus a series of tight back stitching warp threads on a separately weighted beam
consecutive unstitched picks should not exceed twelve

weaves.name: Mock leno (imitation leno)
types: perforated fabrics imitating open gauze effects
distorted thread effects imitating spider or net leno styles

weaves.name: Warp backed
weaves.loom_equipment: Dobby with two warp beams and fast reed
characteristics: two series of warp, one series of weft
face to back warp ratio generally 1:1, sometimes 2:1
warp-faced weaves are suitable; back weave chosen to leave long weft floats on the back

weaves.name: Weft backed
weaves.loom_equipment: Dobby with drop box and fast reed
characteristics: two series of weft, one series of warp
a drop box is required
weft-faced weave is suitable since it has longer warp floats on the back

weaves.name: Weft pile (velveteen)
characteristics: two systems of weft, one system of warp
long floats of weft, cut or uncut - no loops, unlike warp pile
very high weft density: up to 200 picks/cm in the finest fabrics; 50-100 picks/cm for low and medium quality
high weft density achieved by a low warp sett under higher warp tension

weaves.name: Warp pile - Turkish / terry
weaves.loom_equipment: Terry loom with two warp beams and staggering reed
characteristics: pile is NOT cut
one series of weft, two series of warp (ground and pile)
normally formed on 3 picks; 4, 5 and 6 pick structures exist but are costly
ground beam heavily tensioned, pile beam only slightly tensioned
denting order generally two ends per dent (one ground, one pile)

weaves.name: Warp pile - wire pile (velvet)
characteristics: pile formed over a wire inserted across the warp; wire cross-section determines pile height
plain wires give looped pile, bladed wires give cut pile
12 to 50 wires between the point of withdrawal and re-insertion
U binding suits short dense pile; W binding is superior for long pile subject to rubbing

weaves.name: Extra warp figured
weaves.loom_equipment: Dobby/Jacquard with fast reed and two or more warp beams

weaves.name: Double cloth
weaves.loom_equipment: Dobby/Jacquard with fast reed and drop box
characteristics: minimum two series of warp and two series of weft
objectives are thermal resistance and good appearance/feel

constructions.note: warp yarn should have a little more twist than the weft

constructions.cloth: London cord (cotton twill faced Bedford cord)

constructions.weft_count: 60 tex two fold or single cotton / staple viscose rayon

satin_move_numbers.description: Suitable move numbers (intervals of selection) for constructing satin weaves. Reciprocals produce equivalent results. Where more than two intervals are listed, the book marks the best distribution in heavy type.
selection_rules: the move number must not equal the repeat of the weave
it must not be one less than the repeat size
it must not be a factor of the repeat size
it must not be a multiple of a factor of the repeat size

variables.N: number of threads in the repeat of the base twill

broken_twill_skip.constraint: no similar ends must be missed in any two or three consecutive repeats

constraints: repeat size must be a multiple of 4

twill_angle.description: The angle between the diagonal twill line and an axis parallel to the weft, governed by the ratio of ends/inch to picks/inch.

constraints: repeat size must be an odd number
warp float must exceed weft float by one for warp-faced weaves, and vice versa for weft-faced

factors: nature of the yarn - a coarse yarn of lower twist gives a greater twill effect than a fine yarn of higher twist; doubled or ply yarns have a stronger effect than singles
nature of the weave - longer floats give more prominence (3/1 is more prominent than 2/2); an increase in float length must be balanced by proportionately increasing threads/inch
warp and weft threads per inch - prominence increases proportionately with thread density
relative direction of twill and yarn twist - Z twill with Z twist (or S with S) shows LESS prominence; Z twill with S twist (or S with Z) gives MORE prominence

firmness_vs_cover.principle: Firmness depends on the number of intersections. More intersections means better firmness but restricted thread density and less cover; fewer intersections means greater cover through longer floats.

velveteen_shrinkage.note: width-wise shrinkage depends on the weight of the velveteen

depends_on: number of warp ends over which the pile weft floats
velveteen_pile_length.principle: pile length increases with reduced warp thread density per cm, or with an increase in the number of warp threads the pile weft passes over

terry_pile_height.principle: pile height depends on the distance between the fell and the two loose picks (three-pick terry). Higher pile gives a softer feel. Pile yarns are made of lower twist to assist moisture absorption.

wire_pile_depth.note: 1.5 mm for short pile fabrics up to 25 mm for imitation fur fabrics and carpetings

double_cloth_weave_selection.principle: The face and back weaves must have a similar relative number of intersections even when the weaves differ.

reed_and_denting.reed_count_definition: the number of dents in two inches
reed_and_denting.heald_count_definition: the number of heald wires in one inch

light_theory.note: mixing the three primaries in the right proportion produces white

pigment_theory.note: tertiaries are duller than primaries and secondaries because one primary predominates

definitions.tone: results from mixing a colour with white or black
definitions.tint: a lighter tone - a colour mixed with white in different proportions
definitions.shade: a darker tone - a colour mixed with black in different proportions
definitions.coloured_grey: a neutral or broken colour from mixing a normal colour with both black and white in varying proportions
definitions.mode_shade: a broken colour in which a certain hue predominates
definitions.monochromatic_contrast: two tones of the same colour combined
definitions.polychromatic_contrast: two or more different colours combined, alike or different in tone
definitions.successive_contrast: the colours are far enough apart that one is perceived after the other
definitions.simultaneous_contrast: the colours are placed in juxtaposition so both are seen at once
definitions.contrast_of_hue: each colour influences its neighbour - a dark colour makes an adjacent light colour look lighter, and vice versa
definitions.colour_harmony: any combination of hues that is pleasing to the observer
definitions.harmony_of_analogy: combining tones of the same colour that do not differ widely, or closely related hues of equal depth - of chief value for quiet effects
definitions.harmony_of_contrast: combining widely different tones of one colour, or unlike colours - useful for clear and smart effects
definitions.divisional_colours: colours introduced to separate two contrasting colours that would otherwise appear blurred at their joining

visual_effects.red: brilliant and cheerful, gives an impression of warmth, appears to advance towards the observer
visual_effects.blue: a cold colour, appears to recede from the eye
visual_effects.yellow: very luminous and vivid, conveys the idea of purity
visual_effects.orange: very strong, warm and bright, but less intense than yellow
visual_effects.green: retiring and rather cold, but cheerful and fresh
visual_effects.purple: rich and deep, unsurpassed for bloom and softness

factors: manner of arrangement of fibres in the yarn
principles: polyester and viscose have smooth uniform surfaces and give high lustre; irregular twisted fibres such as cotton give poor lustre
filament yarns of low twist present long continuous surfaces and reflect well; spun staple yarns have higher twist, which breaks surface continuity and reduces lustre
a weave with longer floats (such as sateen) presents large continuous areas of yarn and raises lustre
calendering and beetling raise lustre by increasing surface regularity; raising destroys it by disturbing the surface

methods: combining two or more fibre types and dyeing the fabric made from them
printing the spun yarn in different colours
arranging differently dyed yarns alternately and weaving them in an irregular or broken manner
adding small dyed tufts of fibre before spinning, giving a spotted colour effect on the yarn
blending fibres of different colours to produce a mixture yarn
twisting differently coloured threads together to produce fancy yarns
printing slivers in strands of different colours to produce melange yarns

colour_weave_effects.name: Continuous line effect
colour_weave_effects.description: the line produced by the pattern runs lengthwise along the cloth

colour_weave_effects.name: Hound's tooth pattern
colour_weave_effects.description: the classic broken-check figure formed by a 4-and-4 colouring on a 2/2 twill

colour_weave_effects.name: Bird's eye and spot effect
colour_weave_effects.description: the cloth surface is covered with distinct small detached spots of colour; a spot forms where a warp colour is intersected by the same colour of weft

colour_weave_effects.name: Hairline effect
colour_weave_effects.description: solid vertical or horizontal lines, each line one thread wide; wider lines are possible by arranging weave and colouring suitably

colour_weave_effects.name: Step pattern
colour_weave_effects.description: vertical and horizontal lines unite and form zig-zag lines of colour running diagonally; an ordinary twill with equal warp and weft floats is suitable

colour_weave_effects.name: All over effect
colour_weave_effects.description: the colour effect runs unbroken over the surface; the colour-plan repeat and the weave repeat are arranged so two or more weave repeats are needed for one pattern repeat

glossary.definition: A cloth in which alpaca weft is used, with a plain or weft-faced twill weave. Used for dress fabrics and lining cloths.
A 5-end satin fabric with worsted warp and woollen weft, milled and raised to impart a soft feel. Used as dress material.
A fabric constructed with warp rib weave, suitable as a dress fabric.
A silk fabric constructed with an eight-end satin weave. With cotton weft it suits lining cloths.
A light, open cloth woven with plain or 2/2 twill, used for grocery purposes.
Cotton plain cloth finished to give the feel of muslin and cambric. Used for dresses and linings.
A milled and raised woollen fabric made in various weights using backed and double weaves. Used as overcoating.
A fabric with ridges and furrows giving a warp-way stripe resembling cords. Cotton or worsted. Used for dress fabrics and military wear.
Narrow-width fabric of cotton, wool or silk in plain, twill or sateen. Used for skirt tops, ornamentation and power transmission.
A worsted or cotton fabric using a 2/2 twill weave.
A heavy fabric of wool or a wool-cotton admixture; cotton, acrylic and polypropylene are also used.
A milled, raised woollen cloth finished with a fibrous surface. Used for sports jackets and caps.
A woollen cloth milled heavily to impart a felt-like appearance.
An old woollen cloth of fine merino wool in plain weave, heavily milled and finished for dress use.
A heavy silk fabric with figured ornamentation produced on a jacquard.
Cloth passed between heated rollers under pressure, giving a smooth glossy surface. Normally applied to cotton and linen.
Various types of plain woven cotton cloth coarser than muslin.
A cloth of high quality cotton yarn given a special finish for a stiff feel and bright appearance. Used for summer dresses and dress linings.
A plain woven cotton cloth with a soft, full handle.
A silk fabric of very soft filmy texture, made of hard twisted yarn and woven in the gummed condition.
A cloth in which different colours of weft replace one another in succeeding horizontal sections of a design, forming a figure in more colours than there are series of weft threads.
A fabric in which rib effects run longitudinally in the cloth.
A weft pile or velveteen in which the pile forms ribs or cords along the warp direction.
A fine worsted fabric with a warp rib twill effect running at a flat angle.
A fabric with an irregular or broken surface appearance, using a combination of sateen with twill or plain weaves.
A fabric woven with plain, twill, crepe or small fancy weaves, ornamented with elaborate printed designs.
A silk fabric with a weft sateen figure on a warp satin, twill or plain ground.
A strong heavy warp-faced cotton cloth in 3/1 twill. Warp usually dyed brown or blue, weft bleached.
Soft light cotton fabrics 2-5 yards long, with a plain grey body and an ordinary or fancy border.
Warp-faced cotton fabrics in 3, 4 and 5 thread warp-faced twills and 5 thread satin, with twill lines running opposite to the warp twist direction for a prominent twill effect.
A very heavy strong cotton fabric in plain weave. Used for sail cloth, belting and tent cloth.
A fabric similar to denim but usually dyed in both warp and weft.
A woollen cloth subjected to pressure and moisture so the fibres mat and interlock into a dense, full, compact structure.
A plain or twill cloth, generally of woollen yarns, milled and raised to give a very soft handle.
A cotton fabric in plain or 2/2 twill finished with a fibrous surface in imitation of wool flannel.
A velveteen of high pick density, also known as corduroy. Cut weft floats form warp-way fringes giving a rib or cord appearance.
A fabric woven in 2/2 twill construction, commonly of cotton or worsted.
A fabric of open construction resembling a wire mesh.
A fine silk fabric of highly twisted yarns, with S and Z twist arranged 2 and 2 in warp and weft, giving a crepe-like appearance.
A cotton fabric in plain weave with firm texture, normally produced with a check effect.
A cotton or linen cloth used exclusively for cleaning glassware.
The cloth as taken from the loom.
A blended warp rib fabric of fine silk warp with coarser silk, cotton or worsted weft, with high warp density and low pick density.
A simple colour and weave effect producing solid lines warp or weft way; line thickness depends on the thickness and number of coloured yarns.
A plain woven jute cloth produced in a wide range of qualities, used for wrapping and packing.
A worsted cloth woven as 2/2 twill, suitable for coatings and costumes.
A blended cloth with yarn-dyed cotton warp and woollen weft dyed in the fabric state, finished for a lustrous appearance.
A cloth made for military purposes, yellowish brown, made from a mixture of differently dyed fibres.
A net-like fabric made by causing one warp end to cross over another, using doup healds.
A cotton fabric of fine warp and coarse, soft-spun lustrous weft; pick density usually exceeds warp thread density.
A woollen cloth preshrunk by post treatment with hot and cold washes.
A cotton fabric woven as plain in a close texture.
A figured double or treble cloth using wadding threads to give a raised appearance to the figure.
A superfine cotton cloth in plain weave, bleached and finished for a soft feel.
A soft fine fabric of cotton, silk or worsted, woven as plain in an open texture.
A cotton or wool cloth given a raising treatment to make it fibrous or hairy.
Crepe fabrics with a rough texture; the weave is generally irregular.
A fabric characterised by long floats or loops of yarn. Warp pile forms loops (cut or uncut); weft pile forms long floats (cut or uncut).
A weft pile fabric with long floats of weft.
A warp rib cloth with fine warp and coarse weft, made from cotton, wool, silk or a combination.
Figured heavy cotton fabrics using honeycomb, tapestry, repp or alhambra weaves.
A warp rib fabric in which rib lines alternate coarse and fine ends, interlaced by corresponding coarse and fine picks.
Woollen cloths woven as single and double layered structures; single cloths are woven as twills with broad check effects.
A leno structure in which a coloured crossing end crosses over a standard warp end of contrasting colour.
An inferior quality of cotton muslin cloth.
A worsted or woollen cloth in twill construction with a rough feel.
A plain or 2/2 twill fabric of cotton, linen or a polyester-cotton blend, in medium to coarse counts.
A closely sett plain silk fabric using a coarse weft and finer warp.
A woollen or worsted 2/2 twill cloth in elaborate check designs.
A warp pile fabric with loops of warp threads alternating with ground threads. Ideal for towels.
A plain woven cloth of silk or cotton; the cotton version is mercerised and dyed to imitate silk.
A woollen cloth made in forms ranging from fine to coarse textures. Used for suitings and overcoatings.
A warp pile fabric similar to terry but with short cut piles.

primary: shedding - opens the warp sheet into layers to let the shuttle pass
picking - propels the shuttle carrying weft from one end of the loom to the other
beat up - lays the previously laid weft to the fell of the cloth
secondary: take up - winds cloth onto the cloth roller and influences pick density
let off - releases warp from the weaver's beam at a uniform rate, keeping warp tension constant
auxiliary: warp stop motion - stops the loom on warp breakage, preventing missing ends and floats
weft stop motion - stops the loom on weft exhaustion or breakage, preventing cracks
warp protector - prevents multiple warp breakages when the shuttle is trapped in the shed

types.name: Straight draft
types.description: The drafting order progresses successively from the first to the last heald frame. The peg plan is the same as the design, so no separate peg plan is needed.

types.name: Skip draft
types.description: Uses twice or more the minimum number of heald frames to distribute warp threads more uniformly and prevent abrasion from overcrowding. Normally used for plain and twill weaves up to a repeat of 4.

types.name: Sateen draft
types.description: Serves the same purpose as the skip draft, but is used for weaves with a repeat size of more than 5.

types.name: Pointed draft
types.description: The straight draft is reversed after half the repeat warp way. The number of heald shafts is about half the repeat size. Suits pointed twill, diamond weaves and ordinary honeycombs.

types.name: Broken draft
types.description: Resembles the pointed draft but the pointed effect is broken. Suits herringbone twills.

types.name: Divided draft
types.description: Used for weaves having two series of warp threads such as terry, double cloth and warp backed cloth. The two sets are divided into two groups of heald shafts.

types.name: Grouped draft
types.description: Used for stripe and check designs where the stripes have different weaves. The repeat is determined by the number of stripes and the number of threads in each stripe.

types.name: Combined draft
types.description: Two or more draft types applied simultaneously. The most complicated, chosen only where there are technological or economic reasons.
